Record Class TrainingDriver.Outcome

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.micronaut.runner.build.training.TrainingDriver.Outcome
Record Components:
exitStatus - the application's exit status
forced - whether the application did not exit within TrainingSettings.stopTimeout() and was killed
destroyed - whether the driver stopped the application by destroying its process, which is SIGTERM on Linux and macOS, rather than with a stop request or by waiting for it to end by itself
readiness - the time from the launch to readiness; with TrainingSettings.runToExit(), to the exit
total - the time from the launch to the exit
Enclosing class:
TrainingDriver
@Internal public static record TrainingDriver.Outcome(int exitStatus, boolean forced, boolean destroyed, Duration readiness, Duration total) extends Record
How a training run ended.

  • Method Details

    • requireOrderlyExit

      public void requireOrderlyExit() throws IOException
      Fails unless the application shut down in an orderly way: with status 0, or with the status of a JVM that SIGTERM ended when the driver destroyed the process. A run whose stop has to write something, such as a JDK cache, calls this.

      On Windows a destroyed process is terminated without running its shutdown hooks and exits with status 1, so this fails there unless TrainingSettings.stopPath() is set.

      Throws:
      IOException - if the application was killed or exited with another status
